audit_source:
import ErdosProblems.Erdos235

open Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace JSP208Audit

/-- The internal consecutive-gap count, divided by phi of the primorial,
converges to the explicit exponential distribution at every nonnegative c. -/
theorem catalog_limit (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    Tendsto (fun k ↦
      ((Erdos235.internalShortGaps (Erdos235.primeProduct k)
        ⌊c * (Erdos235.primeProduct k : ℝ) /
          ((Erdos235.primeProduct k).totient : ℝ)⌋₊).card : ℝ) /
      ((Erdos235.primeProduct k).totient : ℝ))
      atTop (𝓝 (1 - Real.exp (-c))) := by
  simpa only [Erdos235.gapCDF, Erdos235.normalizedThreshold,
    Erdos235.exponentialGapCDF] using Erdos235.erdos_235_limit c hc

theorem catalog_statement :
    ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, Continuous f ∧ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c →
      Tendsto (fun k ↦
        ((Erdos235.internalShortGaps (Erdos235.primeProduct k)
          ⌊c * (Erdos235.primeProduct k : ℝ) /
            ((Erdos235.primeProduct k).totient : ℝ)⌋₊).card : ℝ) /
        ((Erdos235.primeProduct k).totient : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 (f c)) := by
  simpa only [Erdos235.gapCDF, Erdos235.normalizedThreshold] using Erdos235.erdos_235

#print axioms Erdos235.erdos_235_limit
#print axioms Erdos235.erdos_235
#print axioms catalog_limit
#print axioms catalog_statement

end JSP208Audit
scope: The internal consecutive reduced-residue gap count below a primorial, normalized by phi of that primorial, tends to 1-exp(-c) at every c>=0. The resulting limiting function is continuous. No uniform relative-error rate or prime-gap version is claimed.
scope_review_markdown:
# JSP-000208 / Erdős 235: source-scope review

The source-scope review is supported by the completed run on 2026-09-16: three upstream modules and the typed audit compiled and were individually replayed, all eight processes exiting 0. Both upstream endpoints and both typed statements use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The exact receipts and output-bundle bindings remain the verification evidence; this prose is their scope interpretation.

The [original question](https://www.erdosproblems.com/235), also available in its [LaTeX record](https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/235), asks for existence and continuity of the limiting distribution of normalized internal consecutive gaps between reduced residues below the product of the first k primes. The catalog maps to this question, not to gaps between consecutive primes.

The pinned proof is [Erdos235.lean](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos235.lean). `primeProduct k` multiplies the first k actual primes using Mathlib's increasing prime enumeration. The initial k=0 value is 1 and has no effect on the limit. Positivity of the product and its totient is proved.

`IsInternalConsecutive N a b` requires a<b<N, both endpoints coprime to N and no intermediate coprime integer. Its finite pair set counts each internal gap once. For N>1 the possible a=0 is automatically excluded by coprimality. The natural floor in `normalizedThreshold` exactly matches the real gap inequality at nonnegative c; actual gaps are nonnegative integers. The denominator is phi(N), as in the source question, not the number phi(N)-1 of internal gaps.

The proof first establishes the exponential law for cyclic gaps and then proves the absolute internal/cyclic discrepancy is at most 1/phi(N). The totient tends to infinity, so the missing wraparound gap disappears in the limit. The final `erdos_235_limit` quantifies every real c>=0; c=0 is treated separately. `erdos_235` supplies the continuous function c ↦ 1-exp(-c). There is no unresolved moment, sieve-error or uniformity hypothesis in these endpoints.

Its three-file local dependency closure is CongruenceAverage, Erdos387.BrunSieve and Erdos235. The first supplies finite congruence averaging and imports only Mathlib; the second supplies finite sieve/Bonferroni inequalities and also imports only Mathlib. Importing BrunSieve does not assume any Erdos387 endpoint. No external non-Mathlib package or unproved number-theory input is required by this source closure. The actual endpoint axiom traces report only the standard three axioms; imported Mathlib and standard artifacts remain trusted.

The published reference is Christopher Hooley, *On the difference between consecutive numbers prime to n. II.*, Publicationes Mathematicae Debrecen 12 (1965), 39–49, verified against the [journal record](https://publi.math.unideb.hu/paper/2953), DOI [10.5486/PMD.1965.12.1-4.06](https://doi.org/10.5486/PMD.1965.12.1-4.06). The Lean header credits Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol. This package preserves those credits; it contributes only reproduction and a typed statement audit.

The result covers the original existence-and-continuity question and gives the explicit limiting function. It does not claim the stronger uniform relative-error wording in the webpage's historical commentary, a quantitative convergence rate, or the distinct prime-gap problem 234.
